$comment: EXP-1490 (eMCP E1, epic VAPP-175, 2026-10-31): THE UPSTREAM CONNECTION, one member × one upstream. An UPSTREAM is a team MCP server row (`mcp_servers`, EXP-792) an app names in its package's `upstreams` and binds to (exposes.json `run.upstream`); each MEMBER connects their OWN account (`mcp_credentials`, sealed with the vault, vault.json) and app tools act as the calling member. STATES (`states`, `upstreamStep(state, event)` over `transitions`; `*` = from every state and wins; an event a state does not list changes nothing; no credential and no flow = `disconnected`): `connect` (the member presses Connect: the consent page inline or Settings › MCP › Servers) starts a flow from `disconnected`, `failed`, `reconnect` (or replaces one in `connecting`): the existing `mcp_oauth_flows` (32-byte state, PKCE S256 with the verifier sealed, 10-minute TTL, single use, `return_to` = the page that started it, so the consent page resumes with the server connected); the hosted callback's exchange = `callbackOk` → `connected` or `callbackError` → `failed`; a flow past its TTL = `flowExpired` → `failed`. A `secret` server: `secretSet` → `connected` from anywhere; an `auth: none` server is `connected` without a credential. The access token passing `expires_at` = `expire` → `expired`; the broker refreshes before the call (`refreshOk` → `connected`, `refreshFailed` → `reconnect`); an upstream answering 401/invalid_token to a live token = `unauthorized` → `reconnect`. `disconnect` (the member) and `serverChanged` (an owner retargets the server's url, transport or auth) → `disconnected` from anywhere, the credential row deleted. CALLABLE (`callable`, `callableCases`) = `connected` | `expired`; a binding over any other state answers the error `errors.disconnected`, over a server that no longer exists (removed, or not one of the app's declared `upstreams`) `errors.missing`, and an upstream that fails or times out `errors.failed` (audit status `upstream`). THE CONSENT PAGE (`missingCases`): `missingUpstreams(declared per chosen app, states, existing server names)` = the servers the chosen apps declare that exist and are not callable for this member, sorted, each once; each shows its `labels` state with a Connect action, and the grant saves regardless (tools over an unconnected upstream stay listed and answer `errors.disconnected` until connected). `labels` = the state words every surface shows (Settings › MCP › Servers, the consent page).

binding.$comment: VAPP-230 (eApps M1, apps.md §6.3, C17): A TEMPLATE READS AN UPSTREAM. A binding source `upstream:<server>/<tool>?<args>` (eUI `parseSource`: scheme `upstream`, name = `<server>/<tool>`, split at the LAST `/`, both non-empty; anything else is null) follows one read-only tool of a team MCP server. ARGS (`parseCases`): every query param is one argument; its text reads as JSON when it is `true`, `false`, `null`, a JSON number (`-?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)?([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, so `007` stays text) or starts with `{` or `[` and parses; anything else is the string (so a `bind` action's params drive it, sourceWithParams). DECLARED (`declareCases`, Exponential's install check on top of the SDK's `sources` allowlist): a template binding's server must be in the package's `upstreams` (`notDeclared`), else the install refuses it; a source that does not parse is `invalid`. READS ONLY (`readCases`, checked by the broker at EVERY call against the tool's live `tools/list` annotations): a destructive tool never runs (`destructiveHint: true` or a destructiveWords word in its name, exposes.json: `destructive`); `readOnlyHint: true` reads; `readOnlyHint: false` never reads (`notReadOnly`); a tool that sets no readOnlyHint reads only when the package VOUCHES for it: its `sources` lists the binding's `upstream:<server>/<tool>` EXACTLY (no `*` pattern, no query), else `notReadOnly`. THE BROKER (the server, apps-broker.ts) runs exactly one tool per read as the VIEWING member with their OWN connection (`resolveForLaunch`); an app reaches only its own `upstreams` (the published package's or the head's), never another app's, and nothing chains. CACHE: a good answer is kept `cacheSeconds` per `cacheKey(member, serverId, tool, args)` = the four joined by a newline, args as canonical JSON (audit.json: keys sorted, compact), so the same read by the same member answers from the cache and two members never share one; an error is never cached; hosts re-read every `cacheSeconds` while the binding lives. VALUE (`valueCases`): a result with `isError` is `upstreamFailed`; else `structuredContent` when it is an object; else the first text content parsed as JSON, or that text itself; else null. The answer carries `_meta` provenance (exposes.json keys: app = the app slug, tool = `<server>/<tool>`, via = `upstream`, upstream = the server). HOSTS ×4 (web, desktop, iOS, Android) resolve the `upstream` scheme through ONE call (tRPC `apps.upstreamRead {id, source}` → `{ok: true, value}` | `{ok: false, error, server}`, error ∈ upstream `errors` + `notReadOnly` | `destructive` | `notDeclared` | `invalid`): ok emits the value at the bound path; any refusal or offline emits NOTHING (the path keeps the template's `data`: the binding's default). BANNER (`bannerCases`): the host shows ONE banner per server whose read answered `upstreamDisconnected`, sorted, text `banner` with {server}, its action opening Settings › MCP (the existing host banner); every other error shows none.
